To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the energy density in a cavity with a single moving mirror is obtained by tracing back the null lines from the point of interest to a certain known initial field mode, which is a generalization of previous results in literature.

the quantum radiation force acting on the mirror is proportional to the time-derivative of the instantaneous value of the energy stored in the cavity, and that the energy stored in a cavity is proportional to the energy stored in an infinite space with the same field configuration, but without boundaries, at a certain time in the past.

the exact energy density of the scalar field inside the cavity can be expressed as a function of the initial field modes, and that the quantum force acting upon the mirror is the time derivative of the energy density.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of quantum radiation pressure on a moving mirror, in a cavity with Dirichlet or with Neumann boundary conditions, for an arbitrary initial field configuration, for a finite temperature, and for a coherent state.
the study of the quantum radiation force acting on a moving mirror of a two-dimensional cavity, for a vacuum, a thermal, and a squeezed coherent state, and for arbitrary boundary conditions.

the study of the quantum radiation force on the mirror of a cavity with Dirichlet or a Neumann boundary condition, for a vacuum, a thermal, or a coherent state of the field, in an arbitrary and relativistically allowed law of motion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the quantum radiation force acting on a mirror of a cavity is a well-defined concept, which can be computed exactly for an arbitrary initial field configuration, arbitrary law of motion, and arbitrary boundary conditions, and that it is a nonlocal quantity.
the quantum force acting at the boundary of a cavity, for an arbitrary initial field mode state and arbitrary motion of the boundary, is given by the sum of two contributions.
our formulas are valid for an arbitrary initial state of the field and for arbitrary motion of the boundary.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have obtained the exact value of radiation force on a moving mirror, in the case of Dirichlet and the Neumann boundary conditions, for arbitrary initial field state.
, in the case of a cavity filled with a vacuum or thermal radiation, the quantum radiation force is always attractive.

the quantum radiation pressure is always positive, even for a Neumann boundary condition, and the quantum radiation force is always positive for the Dirichlet boundary conditions and negative for the Neumann ones.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the exact value for the energy density can be found by tracing back the sequence of null lines connecting the given point in the cavity to a known value for the energy, in a way similar to the classical case.
the energy density of a field and the force on a moving boundary can be computed exactly, without any approximations, for an arbitrary law of motion of the mirror.
the energy density and quantum force on the boundaries are not independent of the initial field state.
